findingEvidence.R2F4-1: SqlitePersistenceOptions.testExecutionId and the `test-exec:` path-lock bypass branch removed; the in-process pathLocks map remains with a fixed key (resolved path / per-instance UUID for :memory:), so the production concurrency contract is unchanged. The second real SqlitePersistence in the CAS evidence now runs in a fresh Node child process (tests/helpers/cas-independent-worker.ts) that owns its own module-level pathLocks map and its own DatabaseSync handle: the two submits share no in-process lock and no synchronous connection. Exactly one of the two independent contexts wins; the loser is asserted to have reached the version check and failed closed with DELIVERABLE_VERSION_CONFLICT (SQLITE_BUSY / database-locked outcomes are explicitly NOT accepted as CAS evidence); the shared database holds exactly one evidence link and one submitted action afterwards. Covered by R2F1-4 section 4 and R2F2-4/5 section 4 in tests/deliverable-evidence.test.ts.
findingEvidence.R2F4-2: New frozen module packages/adapters/src/sqlite/schema/v11-schema.ts transcribes the v11 DDL verbatim from base commit 0598ad4 (v1-v10 block, marker rows 2-10, v11 role-slot block, v11 marker) and freezes the v11 reader version guard (v11SchemaVersionGuard: same MAX(version) read + same fail-closed SQLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED contract as the v11 assertSupportedSchema). R2F3-4 now builds its fixture solely from that frozen module via raw DatabaseSync seeding (tenant, principals, memberships, node with leader, asset) — no current v12 adapter creates or strips the fixture. The current SqlitePersistence upgrades v11->v12, is re-instantiated (reopen), and the old v11 rows plus a full init+submit scenario are verified. Old-reader rejection in both R2F2-4/5 and R2F3-4 executes the frozen v11 guard, replacing the previous test-local MAX+manual-throw substitutes.
findingEvidence.R2F4-3: R2F3-1 now reads the post-failure state from the actual executing instance mutatorPersistence (memory: the snapshot-derived MemoryPersistence the handler ran on; sqlite: the fixture persistence the handler ran on), never from the pre-tamper fixture instance. For both backends and both tamper shapes (delete-link / equal-count replace-link) it asserts: aggregate stays submitted at version 2, links/actions unchanged (exactly init+submit, one submitted action), and no NEW event / outbox message / command receipt for this command/event/receipt identity (cmd-accept-r2f3-* / evt:cmd-accept-r2f3-* / accept_deliverable + idem-accept-r2f3-*). To make that direct evidence possible, the transaction-context DomainEventWriter and OutboxWriter ports gained read-only list(tenantId), implemented in both adapters.
